entities.summary: Jacopo Sannazaro was an Italian poet and humanist who played a pivotal role in the revival of classical learning in 15th-century Italy. Born in Naples, Sannazaro was a key figure in the Accademia Pontaniana, a prestigious cultural institution that brought together scholars, poets, and thinkers from across the Mediterranean. His most famous work, “Arcadia”, is a richly detailed and imaginative poem that explores the themes of love, nature, and the human condition. Through his writings, Sannazaro helped to shape the intellectual and artistic landscape of Renaissance Italy, influencing a generation of writers, artists, and thinkers who would go on to shape the course of Western culture. Sannazaro's legacy extends beyond his own work, however, as he also played a significant role in the development of the Italian language and literature, helping to establish Naples as a major center of literary and cultural activity.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Sannazaro's work had a significant impact on the development of the Italian language and literature, helping to establish Naples as a major center of literary and cultural activity. His poem “Arcadia” had a lasting impact on Western literature, influencing generations of writers and thinkers who would go on to shape the course of Western culture.
